items.q: How much does ActiveCampaign cost per month?
items.a: The price depends on contacts, not people: each of ActiveCampaign's four plans includes a fixed number of seats (Starter and Plus one, Pro three, Enterprise five) and then scales up with how many contacts you store, not how many of those seats you actually fill. At the default 1,000-contact tier, that seat allowance comes bundled into $15 a month on Starter up to $145 on Enterprise. Contacts push the bill up far faster than seats do: at 10,000 contacts Starter reaches $149 and Plus $189, and by 50,000 contacts Starter is no longer sold at all, leaving Plus as the cheapest option at $609 a month or Pro at $969 for a team that needs its higher email-send allowance. Decide on seats and automation depth first, then check what your real contact count costs on that plan.

items.q: What's the difference between ActiveCampaign's Starter and Plus plans?
items.a: Starter and Plus differ mainly in automation depth and a few feature gates, not in what they cover. At 1,000 contacts, Starter costs $15 a month against Plus at $49, and a similar gap holds higher up the scale, $149 versus $189 at 10,000 contacts. Starter caps every automation at five actions and includes one user seat with room for one purchased extra; Plus removes that automation-action cap, adds landing pages and standard segmentation, and ships the same CRM and automation engine underneath. ActiveCampaign's Help Center also notes that Starter is a new-signup plan only; an existing ActiveCampaign customer cannot buy it. A solo operator running a handful of simple automations rarely needs what Plus adds; an agency or a business chaining several multi-step automations across triggers usually does, and that need, not contact count, is what should decide between the two plans.

items.q: Will ActiveCampaign charge me more if my contact list grows?
items.a: Yes, but not as a penalty. ActiveCampaign's pricing-page FAQ states that crossing into a higher contact band moves your account to the next band or plan automatically, without locking you out of features or billing a surprise fee. The less obvious limit is how often you email your list, not just its size. ActiveCampaign's plan-comparison table caps monthly email sends at a multiple of contact count: 10 times contacts on Starter and Plus, 12 times on Pro, and 15 times on Enterprise. A 50,000-contact list emailed around twelve times a month adds up to roughly 600,000 sends, past what Plus's allowance covers at that size and in range of what Pro's allowance provides instead. ActiveCampaign has not published whether that multiplier is a hard send cap or a fair-use guideline, so budget one plan tier up if you actually email your full list that often.

items.q: Can I try ActiveCampaign before paying, and what happens after the trial?
items.a: Yes. ActiveCampaign offers a 14-day free trial that needs no credit card to start, and the trial account runs on Pro-plan features regardless of which plan you would actually buy, so you can test advanced segmentation, attribution reporting and the Sales Engagement add-on before committing to any tier. ActiveCampaign's Help Center adds that a Salesforce integration can also be tested during the trial window. What isn't published on ActiveCampaign's pricing page or Help Center is what happens to your account, contacts and automations once those 14 days end without a paid plan in place; neither source states whether data is deleted, frozen or simply locked behind a required upgrade. If you do buy a plan and it turns out to be the wrong fit, the trial isn't the real safety net for that, the 30-day money-back guarantee on paid plans is, since it gives a full refund window well past the trial itself.

items.q: What add-ons and extra fees does ActiveCampaign charge on top of the plan price?
items.a: Several, and none of them has a public price. Every plan beyond Starter's single included seat can add more users, but ActiveCampaign has never published what an extra seat costs, on any plan. The same is true of its enhanced-CRM add-ons, Pipelines and Sales Engagement, both sold on Plus and above; of SMS credits, also sold on Plus and above, which let an account send broadcast text messages; and of the Custom Reports and Transactional Email add-ons available more broadly across the lineup. ActiveCampaign's Help Center confirms each of these exists and lists which plans qualify to buy it, but the actual charge only appears inside the account after you've signed up and started the purchase, not on any page the public can read. That means the plan price you see advertised is a floor, not the full bill, until you've logged in and checked each add-on for yourself.

items.q: Is there a setup fee, and can I get a refund if ActiveCampaign turns out to be the wrong fit?
items.a: No setup fee, and yes, within a window. ActiveCampaign's pricing-page FAQ states there are no setup costs or hidden fees on any plan, and its onboarding-services page adds that onboarding is included free with every paid plan, delivered as a live session or an AI-guided course depending on plan. On the refund side, ActiveCampaign backs every paid plan with a 30-day money-back guarantee: its pricing page states it will give a full refund if you're not satisfied after 30 days. That guarantee, not the 14-day trial, is the real protection against picking the wrong plan, since it applies after a month of real use, not just a trial sample. Neither the pricing page nor the Help Center states whether that refund is prorated for an annual payment made partway through its contract year, so confirm that with ActiveCampaign directly before relying on it late in a paid year.

items.q: Which ActiveCampaign plan should a small business or agency pick?
items.a: It depends on team size and automation complexity more than raw contact count. A solo operator or freelancer with around 1,000 contacts and a few campaigns a month fits Starter, at $15 a month, since its one-seat limit and five-actions-per-automation cap rarely bind at that scale. A small agency or team of two or three, still around 10,000 contacts, usually needs Plus at $189 a month for unlimited automation actions and landing pages, or Pro at $375 with more people actively building campaigns. Once contacts climb toward 50,000, Starter is no longer sold at all, so Plus, at $609 a month, becomes the effective entry point, with Pro at $969 for teams sending past Plus's send-volume allowance. Pick by seats needed and automation complexity; contacts mainly decide which price column you land in once you've settled on a tier.
